findings.title: Cache key uses hash() which is randomized per Python process
findings.body: The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. Python's built-in `hash()` for tuples is randomized per interpreter process (PYTHONHASHSEED). In any multi-process deployment (uWSGI/gunicorn workers), each worker will compute a different hash for the same project set, so cache entries written by one worker will never be read by another. Consequences: (1) the cache provides no benefit across workers — every request is a miss; (2) `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line 67) computes the same randomized hash in its caller, so it cannot invalidate entries created by other workers, making the invalidation function dead in practice. Use a deterministic hash (e.g., `hashlib.sha256` over the joined IDs) or simply stringify the sorted IDs.

findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but never called
findings.body: The helper `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is added but no caller exists in the diff. The function is meant to flush cache entries when the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes, but nothing in the codebase invokes it. As a result, after an admin adds/removes a project from the allowlist, stale `True`/`False` values will be served for up to 60 seconds across the whole worker pool. Either wire it up to the option change handler or remove it. Note: even if it were called, the randomized `hash()` in the key (see other finding) means it would only invalidate entries in the calling process.

findings.title: Tests share the 60s eligibility cache and produce order-dependent results
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the allowlist result in `sentry.utils.cache.cache` for 60s keyed by `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. All four tests in `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest` query the same set of project IDs and only swap `mock_options.get.return_value`. The first test that runs populates the cache (e.g., True for the full allowlist case); subsequent tests that expect the un-upsampled `count == 1` path will instead see the cached True and get upsampled counts of 10, failing. There is no `cache.clear()` in `setUp` and the helper is not patched. Add a cache reset in `setUp` (or key the cache on something that varies per test, e.g. include the option value), otherwise the suite is order-dependent and effectively does not exercise both branches.

findings.title: Public entry point is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects has no direct test
findings.body: The new test file exercises the private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`) but never calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, which is the only function actually used by `OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint._get_event_stats`. The cache hit/cache miss branches and the short-circuit behavior on the cached value are uncovered. Add at least one test that mocks `sentry.utils.cache.cache` and asserts both the cached and uncached paths.

findings.title: _should_apply_sample_weight_transform types dataset as Any instead of ModuleType
findings.body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset: Any, request: Request)` compares `dataset` against `discover`, `errors`, and `transactions` modules. The parameter is typed `Any`, but the caller (`organization_events_stats.py` line 220) passes a module from `sentry.snuba`, and the new module is in the stricter-typing `[[tool.mypy.overrides]]` block in `pyproject.toml`. Type it as `ModuleType` (matching the public `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` signature) so mypy catches accidental non-module values.

findings.title: client_sample_rate accepted without range validation
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` blindly casts `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` to float and stores it as `sample_rate` if truthy. Nothing rejects values outside [0, 1], negative numbers, or NaN. A malformed client sending `client_sample_rate: 100` (or `-1`) will poison `sample_weight` for every event in that project, which then propagates into `upsampled_count()` aggregates (`sum(sample_weight)` in `discover.py`) and silently inflates or zeroes out error counts in dashboards/alerts for allowlisted projects. Add an explicit range check (or coerce/log invalid values) before writing back into `normalized_data`.
